files.purpose: Hydra.swift is the Core model and prompt layer of Hydra, the one-chat-many-heads mode: it defines the persisted pair and head-profile settings (HydraPair, HydraHeadProfile), the per-launch resolution (HydraLaunch with its 8-head uncapped concurrency), the Droppy-run head budget (HydraBudget 24/120/160 tools, 25/35 min, 3 min report), the 25-name dragon roster, the persisted head record (HydraHeadInfo, HydraLanding) and the delegation-round budget (HydraDelegationBudget, maxRefusals 3). Its HydraPrompts enum builds every word the lead and the heads are told: the native and fallback lead policies with their brief, verification, project, auto-merge, review and report-style rules, Claude --agents / Copilot customAgents / Codex config overrides, the merge-state note (mergeStatus), the fenced ```hydra delegation block parser and its sent/leaving markers, the head prompts, and the report message the lead receives. At B3 the auto-merge rule, the failed/held merge-state notes and the report duration format change; everything else is byte-identical and only shifted.

feature_notes: B3 autoMergeRule (708) adds two instructions to the lead: 'if it says Droppy Code retries by itself, say the work lands by itself and ask nothing;' (between the files-remain and merging-failed clauses) and 'A merge never waits on another chat or session: never say it does, and never ask the user to merge.' (before 'If nothing is pending'). The rest of the paragraph is byte-identical. Under OD-0012 F1 both 'Droppy Code' occurrences become 'Marrow' in the port.

B3 mergeStatus .failed (1001-1005) splits on HydraMergeRecord.retryable: when retryable == true it returns 'Merge state: the last try at {time} did not land yet ({detail or "no reason recorded"}). Droppy Code retries it by itself within a minute; nothing is needed from the user, so do not ask for anything or describe it as a problem. Do not claim a successful merge.' Otherwise the text changes from '... is retried once you finish this answer; if the reason needs the user (a sign-in, a conflict), say exactly that.' to '... goes out by itself once that is settled; if the reason needs the user (a sign-in, conflict markers, a real conflict with the remote), say exactly that.' Neither failed form appends the pending sentence (upstream defect 27 still reproduces).

B3 mergeStatus .held (1006-1011) is kept only for records written by earlier versions (comment at 1007): with no unmerged files it returns 'Merge state: nothing from this job is left to merge. Do not claim a new merge or promise another one.'; with files it returns 'Merge state: ' + pendingLine('N files from this job'), i.e. '... is/are not merged yet; it goes/they go out by itself/themselves once you finish this answer with every head back.' The B2 'the merge is waiting at ...' text and its run-on nil-detail fallback 'another chat holds this job's files' are gone.

B3 duration(_:) (1420-1423) replaces the hand-built 'Ns' / 'Mm Ss' with Duration.seconds(Int(seconds)).formatted(.units(allowed: [.seconds, .minutes], width: .narrow, maximumUnitCount: 2, fractionalPart: .hide(rounded: .down))). Integer truncation of the input is unchanged; the rendered text is now produced by Foundation's locale-aware units formatter, so the report header '(<duration>, N tools)' in reportMessage can differ from B2 (for example at exact minutes, where the formatter's default zero-unit handling applies) and in non-English locales. HydraPanel.swift:550 uses the same format style at B3.
Everything from line 1008 (B2) on shifts by +4 lines (B2 1008-1416 -> B3 1012-1420; B2 1419-1434 -> B3 1423-1438); lines 1-1001 keep their numbers.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: the exact en-US (and other-locale) strings Duration.UnitsFormatStyle(.narrow, allowed [.seconds, .minutes], maximumUnitCount 2, fractionalPart .hide(rounded: .down)) produces, e.g. for 59 s, 60 s, 65 s, 120 s and 3,700 s (separator between units, whether a zero seconds unit is hidden). Needs a capture from the macOS reference runtime before the port fixes its fixture; do not assume B2's 'Mm Ss'.

files.purpose: HydraCookbook.swift holds the curated table of ready-made Hydra lead-and-heads pairs offered in the Settings > Hydra cookbook panel. Each HydraPairRecipe names models rather than providers: each side lists the providers that serve its model best first and the catalogue name fragments to look for, with an optional effort and head cap, so the panel can resolve a recipe against whatever providers are set up. The enum also decides whether an asked-for effort is kept (only when the resolved model offers it) and whether a recipe is already added (same two providers and two models, efforts ignored). At B3 the table grows from ten to twelve recipes and the Opus titles say 'Opus 5.5'.

files.purpose: MCP.swift is the Core data model of the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server catalogue: how a server is reached (MCPTransport stdio/http/oauth), which fields the user must fill (MCPField secret/text/path), the seven catalogue categories and their titles, a catalogue entry with its brand tint and sample tools, the resolved launch form (MCPResolvedServer), placeholder filling (fill(_:values:) with the scheme/slash stripping for a host placeholder, oauthURL(values:)), the probe result, the persisted per-server MCPConnection state, the MCPSetupGuide and the MCPConnectionState shown by the page and composer. At B3 the file is purely Core: resolve(values:) and MCPPaths, which reached into MCPProxy and Storage, were moved verbatim to the Services layer.

files.purpose: Timeline.swift defines the persisted document of a chat thread: the TimelineItem stream (user, assistant, reasoning, tool, plan, todos, notice, turnEnd), user messages with Hydra origin markers, queued follow-up prompts with bundles, attachments, tool calls with their 60,000-byte output cap, proposed plans, todos, notices with the usage-limit marker, per-turn TurnRecord and TurnSummary, context usage and the ThreadDocument that wraps them and decodes every list leniently. It also prepares image attachments for providers (base64Images downscales anything above 2000 px on its longest side to a 0.8-quality JPEG through ImageIO, orientation applied) and keeps the HydraMergeRecord log that the lead's merge-state note is built from. At B3 HydraMergeRecord gains an optional retryable flag and its held outcome is documented as legacy-only.

feature_notes: B3 adds 'var retryable: Bool? = nil' to HydraMergeRecord (281-283, doc: a failure that clears by itself and is retried quietly, the forge still checking or a remote that moved; nil on the ones that need the user). It is written true by AppModel+HydraMerge's fail(...retryable: true) and read by HydraPrompts.mergeStatus to pick the 'did not land yet ... retries it by itself within a minute' note. Old documents decode unchanged (absent key -> nil).

B3 rewrites the held doc comment (271-272): 'held is no longer written: a merge never waits on another chat's files now. It stays so records written by earlier versions still decode.' The Outcome enum keeps all five raw values, so B2-era thread documents with held records still load.
TurnRecord, ContextUsage and ThreadDocument are byte-identical and shift by +3 lines (B2 283-366 -> B3 286-369); everything up to line 270 keeps its number.
